one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company event before 2026-12-24 (Q4 FY27 print is due ~early March 2027). Window drivers: (a) post-earnings drift after an -18% print-day fall (218.37 -> 179.01, src 13) on a FY28 FTTH guide-down; DY's own 2018-19 guide-downs kept drifting lower over following weeks (src 11, 12); (b) sell-side target cuts and estimate revisions still to land (consensus feeds unrevised as of 2026-11-25, src 6/7), as after Q2 when KeyBanc/Cantor cut ~30% (src 10); (c) December tax-loss selling in a name down ~45% over the year; offsets: $200M buyback authorization and insider buying earlier in the fall (src 9), oversold bounce. Median set slightly below spot at $176 with sigma 0.175 (59%/3.5 = 0.169, nudged for fat tails).

fair_value.method: Driver build (Comms core + long-haul/DCI + Building Systems, segment adj. methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM adj. inputs_detail.derivation: FY27: Comms ~$6,027M (YTD reported plus Q4 at the seasonal Q4 share; inside the $6.00-6.04B guide, src 2) less est. LH/DCI $250M. inputs_detail.derivation: Base/FY27 split of 'several hundred millions over 2 years' (~$400M) as $150M/$250M. downside.story: P10: FTTH customers cut FY28 builds further (core Comms -7% vs base), LH/DCI ramps slower, a data-center pause or local moratoria trims BS 12%, Comms margin -150bp on deleverage and more customer credit losses, BS margin -300bp; P/E de-rates ~3 turns toward DY's 2019 trough. Base rate: after the Aug-2018 and Feb-2019 guide-downs DY fell a further ~45% over 12 months. A second base rate (MasTec 2023) shows reset contractors can re-rate fast when a new end market (power/data center) carries growth, so the left tail is not wider than the right in price terms.

upside.story: P90: FTTH pause is short, BEAD construction starts, LH/DCI converts faster, BS grows ~29%, Comms margin returns to ~13.2%; the multiple recovers ~3 turns toward the peer median, as MasTec did within 12 months of its Oct-2023 guidance cut (from ~$47 to $144, src 26, 27).

reasoning: Round 2. Base rates: DY fell 18% on the Q3 print (218.37 -> 179.01) after an August reset and is 68% off its high. Two precedents now anchor the range: DY's own Aug-2018/Feb-2019 guide-downs ($89 Jul-2018 -> $45 Feb-2019, still $44.5 Aug-2019, src 11, 12) show a reset contractor staying de-rated for a year; MasTec's Oct-2023 guide cut (-20% to $47.29, src 26) was followed by a re-rating to $144.06 by Nov-2024 (src 27) once power/data-center work carried growth. So the median keeps 80% of DY's discount (k=0.8) but the upside case adds 3 turns. Supervisor findings acted on: (1) the exit multiple now prices DY and the four whole-company peers on one date (2026-11-24 closes, src 21) and one feed vintage (2026-11-25): peer median 14.63x, DY 10.20x -> 10.96x (was 11.35x on mixed dates); (2) the supplier finance check is closed from XBRL: 524.0M at 2026-10-31 (src 25), half treated as debt-like (-262, -$8.87/share); (3) Building Systems FY28 rebuilt from the Q3 exit rate ($1,767M annualized) plus ~11% crew adds = $1,966M (+17%, was +15%), 66% covered by the $1.3B 12-month backlog; (4) added Verizon's net-90 payment terms (src 29) to long-dated risks. I keep my own Comms build (FY28 +3.5% total, below the CEO's mid-single-digit read; FY29 +6.9%, accelerating as he says) and the 24.5% tax rate on the GAAP-rate history; I disagree with the supervisor's 13.0x exit because it reads DY's own multiple at the 2026-11-02 price, before two resets the market has since priced, and the k rule is about today's gap. Macro odds (Kalshi 2027 recession 20%, src 20; fed funds above 4% through Oct 2027, src 14) keep carriers' cost of capital high, so no quick FTTH re-acceleration. Result: research target (12m) $237.18 (P/E $227.62, EV/EBITDA $259.49), P10 $107.22, P90 $382.20.
